_note: AI-drafted Call to Worship — pending Wilson's curation.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Clap your hands, all peoples; shout to God with songs of joy!
God has gone up with a shout, the Lord with the sound of the trumpet.
He lifted his hands and blessed them, and was carried into heaven,
and they worshiped him and returned with great joy.
Why do you stand looking up? He will come as he went.
Far above all rule and power, he is seated, and the church is his body.
Lift up your hearts to the risen and reigning Lord.
Sing praises to our King, sing praises!

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Watch his hands go up over them in blessing, the last thing they see before the cloud takes him in.
Sing praises to our King, sing praises!
They stand on the hill with their faces lifted to an empty sky, and two messengers ask: why are you still looking up?
Sing praises to our King, sing praises!
He has not gone far off; he is seated above every rule and power, and the whole church is his living body on the earth.
Sing praises to our King, sing praises!
So they go down the mountain not grieving but glad, into the city, into the waiting, into the joy.
Sing praises to our King, sing praises!
Clap your hands, all you peoples, and lift the shout that fills the heavens:
Sing praises to our King, sing praises!

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: He lifts his hands in blessing, and the cloud takes him home.
Sing praises to our King, sing praises!
Why look up? He reigns above every power, and we are his body.
Sing praises to our King, sing praises!
They come down the mountain with great joy.
Sing praises to our King, sing praises!
Clap your hands, all peoples; come, let us worship.
Sing praises to our King, sing praises!
